name: Fuzzy Match
description: Finds near-duplicate records within one input (with group IDs), or the best matching record in a second input, using fuzzy text similarity.
introductoryText:
Finds records that refer to the same thing even when they are written differently: "Acme Widgets Ltd", "ACME Widgets Limited" and "Acme Widget Ltd.".

**One input connected: de-duplicate.** Every record gets a *Group ID*; records that match each other (directly or through a chain of matches) share it. The first record of each group is marked as the group master.

**Two inputs connected: lookup.** Every record of the first input gets its best match (or best few) from the second input, such as invoices matched to a supplier master list, with the matched fields appended.

Text is normalised first (case, accents, punctuation, "&" vs "and", and optionally company suffixes such as Ltd, Limited, plc, Inc). Choose a similarity measure, a threshold, an optional second field (for example the address) and an optional field that must match exactly (for example the postcode), which also speeds up large inputs.

The second output lists every matching pair with its score, for review and audit.

Pure Python: no packages to install.

options.name: match_field
options.title: Match field
options.description: The text field to compare, such as a company or customer name.

options.name: reference_field
options.title: Match field in second input
options.description: Lookup mode only. Leave empty to use the field with the same name as the match field.

options.name: second_field
options.title: Second field to compare (optional)
options.description: An extra field compared with the same measure, such as an address line. Blended into the score using the weight below.

options.name: second_reference_field
options.title: Second field in second input
options.description: Lookup mode only. Leave empty to use the field with the same name.

options.name: second_weight
options.title: Weight of second field
options.description: Share of the score that comes from the second field, from 0 to 1.

options.name: block_field
options.title: Must match exactly (optional)
options.description: Only records with the same value in this field are compared, such as postcode or country. Improves precision and speeds up large inputs.

options.name: block_reference_field
options.title: Must match exactly, second input
options.description: Lookup mode only. Leave empty to use the field with the same name.

options.name: algorithm
options.title: Similarity measure
options.description: How the similarity of two values is scored, from 0 (nothing in common) to 1 (identical after clean-up).

choices.title: Jaro-Winkler, any word order (recommended for names)

options.name: threshold
options.title: Match threshold
options.description: Pairs scoring at or above this value count as a match. 0.85 to 0.92 suits company names.

options.name: max_matches
options.title: Matches per record (lookup mode)
options.description: How many of the best matches to return for each record of the first input.

options.name: normalise
options.title: Ignore case, accents and punctuation
options.description: Compare "Café & Co." and "cafe and co" as the same text.

options.name: ignore_suffixes
options.title: Ignore company suffixes
options.description: Drop words such as Ltd, Limited, plc, LLP, Inc, Corp, Co, GmbH and The before comparing.

options.name: ignore_words
options.title: Other words to ignore
options.description: Comma-separated words to drop before comparing, such as services, group.

blockOutputs.label: Matched
blockOutputs.tooltip: De-duplicate: the input with Group ID, Group Size, Is Group Master and Best Match Score. Lookup: the first input with the best match from the second input appended.

blockOutputs.label: Pairs
blockOutputs.tooltip: Every pair scoring at or above the threshold, with both values and the score.
